The '''''ATLAS of Finite Groups''''', often simply known as the '''''ATLAS''''', is a [[group theory]] book by [[John Horton Conway]], [[Robert T. Curtis|Robert Turner Curtis]], [[Simon P. Norton|Simon Phillips Norton]], [[Richard A. Parker|Richard Alan Parker]] and [[Robert Arnott Wilson]] (with computational assistance from [[J. G. Thackray]]), published in December 1985 by [[Oxford University Press]] and reprinted with corrections in 2003 ({{ISBN|978-0-19-853199-9}}).<ref name="Breuer2017">{{Cite book |first1=Thomas |last1=Breuer |arxiv=1603.08650 |chapter=Reliability and reproducibility of Atlas information |first2=Gunter |last2=Malle |first3=E. A. |last3=O'Brien |title=Finite Simple Groups: Thirty Years of the Atlas and Beyond |publisher=American Mathematical Society |pages=21–32 |year=2017 |isbn=978-1-470-43678-0 |series=Contemporary Mathematics |volume=694}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Curtis |first=Robert T. |title=John Horton Conway, 26 December 1937 — 11 April 2020 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=72 |pages=117–138 |year=2022 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2021.0034|doi-access=free }}</ref> The book codified and systematized mathematicians' knowledge about [[finite group]]s, including some discoveries that had only been known within Conway's group at [[Cambridge University]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Brian |last=Denton |title=none |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |volume=70 |number=453 |page=248 |date=October 1986 |doi=10.1017/S0025557200139440 }}</ref> Over the years since its publication, it has proved to be a landmark work of mathematical exposition.<ref name="Breuer2017"/>

It lists basic information about 93 finite [[simple group]]s. The [[classification of finite simple groups]] indicates that any such group is either a member of an infinite family, such as the [[cyclic group]]s of prime order, or one of the 26 [[sporadic group]]s. The ''ATLAS'' covers all of the sporadic groups and the smaller examples of the infinite families. The authors said that their rule for choosing groups to include was to "think how far the reasonable person would go, and then go a step further."<ref>''ATLAS,'' p. vii.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|jstor=2322937 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=93 |number=10 |date=December 1986 |pages=C85–C91 |first1=Lynn Arthur |title=none |last1=Steen |display-authors=etal}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first=R. |last=Steinberg |title=none |journal=Mathematics of Computation |volume=48 |number=177 |date=January 1987 |page=441 |doi=10.2307/2007904 |jstor=2007904}}</ref> The information provided is generally a group's order, [[Schur multiplier]], [[outer automorphism group]], various constructions (such as [[Presentation of a group|presentations]]), conjugacy classes of [[maximal subgroup]]s, and, most importantly, [[character table]]s (including power maps on the conjugacy classes) of the group itself and bicyclic extensions given by stem extensions and automorphism groups.  In certain cases (such as for the [[Group of Lie type|Chevalley groups]] <math>E_n(2)</math>), the character table is not listed and only basic information is given.

The ''ATLAS'' is a recognizable large format book (sized 420&nbsp;mm by 300&nbsp;mm) with a red cardboard cover and spiral binding.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1090/bull/1744 |first1=R. L. |last1=Griess |author-link1=Robert Griess |title=Selected Mathematical Reviews related to the work of John Horton Conway |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |display-authors=etal |volume=58 |number=3 |pages=443–456 |date=July 2021 |doi-broken-date=25 February 2026 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2021-58-03/S0273-0979-2021-01744-7/S0273-0979-2021-01744-7.pdf}}</ref><!---This is worth mentioning because the ATLAS's appearance is very striking and easily memorized as it is often seen apart from other books in math libraries.---> (One later author described it as "appropriately oversized".<ref>{{cite journal|first=Peter |last=Sin |title=none |doi=10.4169/000298910x496804 |journal=American Mathematical Monthly |year=2010 |volume=117 |number=7 |pages=657–660}}</ref> Another noted that his university library shelved it among the oversized geography books.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-finite-simple-groups |website=MAA Reviews |publisher=Mathematical Association of America |access-date=29 April 2024 |date=30 March 2010 |first=Felipe |last=Zaldivar |title=The Finite Simple Groups}}</ref>) The cover lists the authors in alphabetical order by last name, each name having six letters, which was also the order in which the authors joined the project.<ref>''ATLAS,'' p. xxxii.</ref> The abbreviations by which the authors refer to certain groups, which occasionally differ from those used by some other mathematicians, are known as "''ATLAS'' notation".<ref>{{cite journal|first=R. L. |last=Griess |author-link=R. L. Griess |title=My Life and Times with the Sporadic Simple Groups |journal=  Notices of the International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians|date=July 2021 |pages=11–46 |volume=9 |number=1 |url=https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/iccm/2021/0009/0001/ICCM-2021-0009-0001-a002.pdf |doi=10.4310/ICCM.2021.v9.n1.a2}}</ref>

Liebeck]]|author20=[[A. Shalev]]|author21=[[K. Lux]]|author22=[[M. Wiegelmann]]|author23=[[V. D. Mazurov]]|author24=[[V. I. Zenkov]]|author25=[[S. P. Norton]]|author26=[[R. A. Parker]]|author27=[[W. Plesken]]|author28=[[Robert Arnott Wilson|R. A. Wilson]]|author29=[[F. Zara]]|url=http://archive.org/details/isbn_9780521575874 |title=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series, Series Number '''249''' The Atlas of Finite Groups: Ten Years On |date=1998 |publisher=[[The Press Syndicate of the University of Cambridge]]|publication-place=[[The Pitt Building]], [[Trumpington Street]], Cambridge, CB2 1RP  |editor1=[[Robert Curtis (mathematician)|Robert Curtis]]|editor2=Robert Wilson|isbn=978-0-521-57587-4 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> It was the subject of an [[American Mathematical Society]] symposium at [[Princeton University]] in 2015, whose proceedings were published as ''Finite Simple Groups: Thirty Years of the Atlas and Beyond''.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bhargava |first1=Manjul |url=https://www.ams.org/books/conm/694/conm694-endmatter.pdf |title=Finite Simple Groups: Thirty Years of the Atlas and Beyond |last2=Guralnick |first2=Robert |last3=Hiss |first3=Gerhard |last4=Lux |first4=Klaus |last5=Pham |first5=Huu Tiep |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2017 |isbn=9781470436780 |location=Princeton NJ}}</ref>
